parsed.explanation: Sodomy law is secondary for trans visitors, but it functions as a documented police lever: some LGBTQ people were arrested on gender-identity grounds after attackers invoked their status, and the law deters victims from reporting — police are not a reliable protector. Social hostility is documented (fliers, sentiment, concealment as the norm), and legislative pressure is active and worsening (2024 bill, harsher proposals), raising severity-if-outed. Positives: enforcement of the sodomy law uncommon, no trans-specific presentation offence documented, no universal facility/custody exclusion, no documented trans-specific violence pattern, and private spaces exist. The employment statute is resident-facing. No care access matters only if a visitor needs refills; unknown rather than exposure. Net: hostile climate and thin recourse without documented universal exposure or organised targeting — elevated risk.
